A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RadarGen and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched despite extensive reformatting and changed figure/table numbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original MAN TruckScenes generation experiments, conditioning and reconstruction ablations, qualitative examples, and downstream detection results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds nuScenes experiments, mixed real/synthetic detector training, and range-image reconstruction tests.

M1.justification: The BEV radar representation, foundation-model conditioning, SANA denoiser, and IRL1/FISTA point recovery remain unchanged. The added timestamp explanation and experiments do not establish a revised RadarGen procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix C.5 adds training and evaluation on nuScenes, extending the previous MAN TruckScenes coverage to a different vehicle/sensor setup with five radars and substantially sparser point clouds. The existing driving scenarios and nighttime example are retained.

E2.justification: Appendix C.6 newly evaluates LiDAR Diffusion's pretrained autoencoder in a radar range-image reconstruction comparison. This is a component-level comparator, not a full generation baseline. RGB2Point and the existing conditioning/recovery comparators remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds a distinct detector evaluation design: training with real or synthetic inputs selected with 50% probability and testing on real data. New reconstruction tests use 96 x 1024 range images on MAN TruckScenes mini-train; the nuScenes RGB2Point output is set to 208 points. Existing metric definitions and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C.6 adds quantitative and visual tests of whether SANA and LiDAR-specific autoencoders preserve sparse radar range images, directly examining the representation choice. Appendix C.4 adds a detector-training compatibility analysis. Existing conditioning, bandwidth, recovery, seed, and nighttime analyses remain.

E5.justification: The captions of main Tables 1 and 2 now identify the existing entries as mean plus/minus standard deviation across timestamps or foreground objects. This clarifies statistical reporting; the PDFs do not report additional repeated training runs, changed seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds nuScenes results, including RadarGen versus RGB2Point CD Loc. of 3.50 versus 3.85 and foreground hit rate of 0.49 versus 0.18. It also reports mixed-training NDS of 0.48 and range-image reconstruction CD increases from 0.31 to 3.72 m with SANA and 0.28 to 4.91 m with the LiDAR autoencoder. All three v1 tables retain identical numerical values in their matched v2 tables.

T1.justification: The conditioning mathematics, nonnegative deconvolution objective, and Appendix A metric definitions are unchanged. The new range-image discussion supplies empirical evidence and conceptual reasoning, without adding formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about probabilistic camera-conditioned radar generation, BEV conditioning, evaluation metrics, and perception/editing applications. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges that it does not model radar's physical mechanisms and explains the missing raw-data/specification requirements. Appendix C.6 explains limitations of range-image smoothing and pretrained autoencoder reuse. C.4 interprets mixed-training parity as compatibility while leaving improved augmentation performance to future work.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 newly specifies approximately 0.1-second MAN TruckScenes frame intervals and computation of actual intervals separately for each frame pair and camera view. Settings for the added experiments are documented, while existing optimizer, hardware, inference, and recovery details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography retains the same works, but Appendix C.6 develops the comparison with previously cited LiDAR Diffusion, explaining why radar adaptation requires a different autoencoder and RCS/Doppler outputs. The broader related-work organization and novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited grammatical corrections, clarifies introductory motivation and notation, updates acknowledgments, and adds appendix subsections C.5 and C.6. Most prose and the main section sequence are retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation, extensively resizing and relocating figures and tables. v2 adds a LiDAR/radar comparison figure, a nuScenes table and qualitative figure, and a range-image reconstruction figure. Existing appendix Figures 7–12 are retained as supplementary Figures 1–6.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens v1's single-dataset validation and its justification for BEV over range images. The nuScenes evaluation tests substantially sparser radar data, while the two autoencoder reconstruction tests directly support a central design choice. Statistical clarification and mixed-training evaluation improve interpretation. The gains concern evidential support: mixed training only matches real-only NDS, and nuScenes split details remain underspecified.
